summary: Idaho-Montana ridge lookout with an L-4 cab in the 1930s, destroyed 1962 per Idaho sources; a September 2025 post found no remains.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1962 per Idaho sources; a Montana list says removed. A September 2025 post found no remains.

visit.trail_note: Listed as a hike-in; the summit is a short walk from State Line Road (climbing guide).

evidence.supports: Site on the Idaho/Montana border, on the ridge crest south of Dominion Peak
evidence.quote: Crittenden Peak sits on the Idaho/Montana border on a section of the ridge crest south of Dominion Peak.

evidence.supports: Named after one of the first Forest Service volunteers in the area
evidence.quote: Crittendon Peak was named after one of the first Forest Service volunteers of this area.

evidence.supports: The namesake did not return from World War I
evidence.quote: He did not return from WWI.

sources.title: Crittenden Peak - IDAHO: A Climbing Guide

corrections.why: The Idaho pages name the St. Joe National Forest, and firelookout.com names both forests. The record lists only Lolo. The editor should confirm.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Idaho sources date the destruction to 1962. The Montana list says removed. The story reports both.
Idaho pages say St. Joe National Forest, the Montana list says Lolo National Forest, and firelookout.com names both. The story reports the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Elevation is 6,416 feet, about 1,956 m; elevation_m is null in the record and has no facts key. No source gives a tower height, so height_m is not set. All sources date the L-4 cab only to the 1930s, so no built event is set because events need a year. The Idaho pages say no staffing history is documented, so no staffing names are given beyond the unstaffed status after 1962. The Montana list and the 1962 date disagree on the fate; the story keeps both. Spelling: the record and most pages use Crittendon, while the climbing guide uses Crittenden. Notable fires: none in these sources.
